summary: Configured a dedicated node2 uploader identity that submits newline-delimited batches to node1 through a forced SSH command. Each submission becomes one atomic, byte-exact receipt. Arbitrary commands, shells, PTYs, and forwarding are denied. Existing data, administrative SSH behavior, RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1, SELinux, firewall, and packages were preserved. Both nodes passed isolated restart and recovery testing.
actions_performed: Created locked `ingest` and `uploader` application accounts, separate from administrative access.
Generated and securely stored an ED25519 key on node2; pinned node1’s verified host key.
Installed a root-owned atomic receiver and public-key-only SSH policy with forced command and forwarding/TTY restrictions.
Verified allowed submission using `runuser -u uploader -- ssh node1-ingest < batch-file`.
Verified command, shell, PTY, and forwarding denial through the intended key.
Created three byte-identical verification receipts; retained the original sample and prior receipt unchanged.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.
Removed temporary test processes and files; installed no packages or upgrades.
